rationale: E2.3 review fix (P0-7): lease.CreateRecord's write-once install moved off a direct O_CREAT|O_EXCL open on record.json's own final path, which made write-once a syscall guarantee one syscall too early — a crash between that open and its write left EXACTLY the corrupt/partial file a reader must never see, present and EEXIST-able before a single byte of its content existed. writeRecordOnce now writes the full content to a same-directory 0600 temp file, fsyncs and closes it, and only THEN installs it via os.Link (never os.Rename): link(2), like the O_EXCL open before it, refuses rather than replaces an existing target, so write-once stays exactly the same syscall-level guarantee, just reachable only once the content it publishes is already durable. The identity-match check that used to run only before a create attempt is now the shared checkExistingRecord, reused after a lost create race too: the old EEXIST branch was a bare `return readRecordFile(path)` with no validation, silently handing a racing caller asking for a DIFFERENT instance id the WINNER's record as if it were its own.

E2.5 escalation (BLOCK 3): RunSession's lease-failure fallback is DELETED. It used to warn and then spawn spec.CreateArgs with no lease at all — after the cutover that is a second, selectable create path (the exact thing PRD §8 forbids), and it created a sandbox nothing on this host could prove it owned. A lease/state-dir failure is now a hard SessionRefused before anything spawns, so the literal `return child.Wait()` that belonged to that fallback is gone; the invariant this pin exists for is untouched and still pinned by the two surviving literals (the transition runs inside AttachRefUnderLifecycle's fn, and the child is waited for only after the refs reference is held).

rationale: E2.5 escalation (BLOCK 6): the create no longer merely RECORDS a lease, it PROMOTES the bounded create intent into the instance-bound, write-once receipt (E2.3's PromoteCreateIntent), which binds instance id AND name and clears the intent. Recording therefore happens only on the create path's own promotion step, so startSessionTransition's attach branch no longer computes `recorded := SessionRecorded(spec.Key)` for a create it does not perform — it consults SessionRecorded only to decide whether -k/--keep has a record to bind to. The verified-instance-id requirement this pin exists for is unchanged and still pinned by the two surviving literals, and is now additionally enforced in PromoteSessionCreation.

rationale: Stale pin, not a behavior change: ExecArgv already places the replayed command after a literal `--` separator (docs/design/pix-v2-architecture.md §6.3, so an in-sandbox flag like --model/--resume is never ambiguous with sbx's own flags) and this pin's `services/host/sandbox/argv.go` literal predates that separator. Updated to match the shipped argv exactly; nothing in ExecArgv's behavior moved this commit.

SECURITY/QA re-review F1 (real behavior fix, not a stale pin): an attach used to replay the STORED create-time invocation (readSessionInvocation) verbatim, silently ignoring a NEW --model/--resume the user asked for on this exact run — verified live: attaching with --model google/gemini-3.1-pro --resume sess-456 exec'd the create-time anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 + sess-123 instead. docs/design/pix-v2-surface.md §3.1 ("both options apply to every attach") and `pix help run` ("--model is NOT create-only") both promised the opposite. Fixed: startSessionTransition's attach branch now always execs spec.DefaultInvocation (this call's own current, freshly resolved invocation); the stored invocation remains an audit trail only (reap.go's own read of it is unchanged).

rationale: Round-4 config collapse (destructive cutover, no released users): config.toml's schema is now pixhome.Machine alone (default_environment + memory_port). config.Config keeps only the launcher-runtime keys, and its `services`, `mcp`, `packs`, and `pack` keys are DELETED along with the legacy Save path, the `pix config` verb, mcp.RegisterServers' pack-manifest registration admin, and the onboarding.json host-config write path. The environment's .sbxenv.yaml plus the reserved built-ins are the ONE MCP declaration channel, so config.toml can no longer smuggle a second one into a launch.

rationale: Wave B/D coexistence: `pix rm --all` discovery is now STACK-SCOPED, not merely pix-* scoped. One PIX_HOME = one stack (a 16-hex id derived from the canonical PIX_HOME path), every sandbox name carries it, and the bulk sweep iterates workspace.ParseScopedBoxes(raw, stackID) — pix-* AND this stack's id — so a `pix reset`/`pix rm --all` run from one PIX_HOME can never remove a coexisting PIX_HOME's sandboxes. The old literal pinned the UNSCOPED ParsePixBoxes discovery loop, which is exactly the behavior this change forbids; the keep POLARITY the rule exists for (`if !keep[b.Name] {`) is unchanged and still pinned.
evidence: services/host/workflow/launch/sandbox.go (RmAll's ParseScopedBoxes discovery); services/host/workspace/sandboxls.go (ParseScopedBoxes); services/host/stack/names.go (IsScopedSandboxName); services/host/cmd/pix/reset_cmd_test.go (TestResetCmd_SweepIsScopedToCurrentStack)

rationale: Wave B/D coexistence: the sandbox identity that keys lease/keep/fingerprint state is now derived from this PIX_HOME's stack id as well as the workspace digest. resolveSandboxName resolves stack.Current() FIRST and routes both branches through it (sandbox.NameForStack for the default, sandbox.ScopeExplicitName for an explicit --name), so an explicit name no longer travels verbatim and an underivable stack id is an error rather than an unscoped fallback. launch.SessionName's old one-line sandbox.Name(workspace) form is gone from the production path — it survives only as a panicking test shim — so the rule now pins the REAL caller in cmd/pix and asserts the old unscoped one-liner is absent.
